key_insight: Sparse long-range (power-of-two) circuit connectivity can expand the accessible operator space in variational quantum algorithms, but greater expressibility alone does not guarantee better trainability or task performance.
engineering_relevance: For neutral-atom and trapped-ion hardware, circuit geometry and qubit reconfigurability should be treated as task-dependent design resources when choosing ansätze for optimization.
method: Dynamical Lie-algebra analysis of accessible operators
Approximate unitary-design diagnostics plus finite-depth expressibility/entanglement measures
Benchmarking variational performance on example target problems with and without long-range couplings
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative evaluation across structured sparse long-range graphs and local circuits, showing that increased connectivity broadens the reachable space but does not universally improve optimization outcomes.
watch_item: Long-range connectivity increases circuit complexity and may not yield a trainable advantage unless the ansatz is matched to the target Hamiltonian or problem structure.
paper_title: Variational Learning with Sparse Long-range Entangling Gates
